title: Sitcom about six close-knit young adults balancing love, work, and friendship in New York City

clues.text: A beloved 1990s ensemble comedy that became a global cultural touchstone influencing slang and fashion trends.
It ran for 10 seasons on a major U.S. network from 1994 to 2004.
Primarily set in Manhattan, with a signature coffeehouse hangout featuring a comfy orange couch.
Famous for catchphrases like “How you doin’?” and the ongoing debate about being “on a break.”
Its finale drew over 50 million U.S. viewers, and guest stars included Brad Pitt, Julia Roberts, and Bruce Willis.

title: Epic fantasy drama about rival noble families battling for power across a brutal medieval realm while an ancient menace gathers in the frozen north

clues.text: Adapted from a bestselling fantasy novel series known for intricate politics and shocking character deaths.
Debuted in 2011 and rapidly became a global phenomenon, breaking viewership records and winning dozens of major awards.
Renowned for cinematic-scale battles and expansive location filming across Northern Ireland, Croatia, Spain, and Iceland.
Centers on warring houses contesting a coveted throne, with dragons, direwolves, and a looming threat from beyond a massive ice barrier.
Iconic characters like Jon Snow, Daenerys Targaryen, Tyrion Lannister, and Arya Stark entered mainstream pop culture lexicon.

title: Slick mystery series about a brilliant consulting detective and his loyal doctor friend solving crimes in modern London.

clues.text: A globally popular British crime drama that relocates a legendary detective to present-day London.
Recognized for stylized on-screen deductions, rapid texting visuals, and “mind palace” sequences that map the detective’s thoughts.
Produced by the BBC and co-created by Steven Moffat and Mark Gatiss, with Gatiss portraying the detective’s government-official brother.
Known for its unusual format of three feature-length episodes per series, plus a 2016 Victorian-set special.
Stars Benedict Cumberbatch as the titular sleuth and Martin Freeman as his doctor companion, with Andrew Scott’s acclaimed turn as Moriarty.

title: Gritty crime drama about a desperate teacher and his former student who turn to manufacturing drugs to secure their futures.

clues.text: Became a global phenomenon for its nerve‑shredding tension and a lead character’s descent from family man to feared antihero.
Set in Albuquerque, New Mexico, featuring stark desert vistas and an RV that served as an early mobile lab.
Its signature blue product became a pop‑culture icon, spawning themed candy and merchandise.
Expanded into a critically acclaimed prequel centered on a fast‑talking lawyer, plus a 2019 epilogue film.
Won 16 Primetime Emmys; fans recall the alias “Heisenberg,” the line “I am the one who knocks,” and the famous hat‑and‑goatee silhouette.

title: Supernatural coming-of-age saga about a tight-knit group of kids, teens, and their families battling mysterious forces in a small Midwestern town.

clues.text: A global streaming phenomenon blending sci-fi, horror, and coming-of-age drama, set in the 1980s.
Known for its retro aesthetics and synth-driven score, it reignited worldwide nostalgia for 1980s pop culture.
Centers on a group of young friends, older siblings, and anxious parents confronting government secrets and otherworldly threats.
A 2022 storyline pushed Kate Bush’s 1985 song back to the top of international charts.
Key elements include a girl with telekinetic powers named Eleven, the town of Hawkins, and a deadly parallel realm called the Upside Down.

title: Sitcom about brilliant but awkward roommates whose lives collide with their outgoing neighbor

clues.text: Ensemble comedy about socially inept physicists whose tight-knit friendship is tested and enriched by new relationships.
Helped mainstream geek culture with constant nods to comic books, cosplay, video games, and real scientific concepts.
Regularly featured celebrity cameos from science and tech icons, including Stephen Hawking, Bill Gates, and Stan Lee.
Its success led to a hit prequel focusing on the childhood of one central character.
Aired on CBS for 12 seasons (2007–2019), popularized the catchphrase “Bazinga!”, and centered on Sheldon, Leonard, and Penny.

title: Anthology drama about ordinary people pushed to extremes by near-future technology and media-fueled anxieties

clues.text: Anthology series that explores the unsettling consequences of modern technology on everyday life.
Created by Charlie Brooker, it began on Channel 4 before moving to Netflix and finding a massive global audience.
Critically acclaimed standalone episodes include “San Junipero,” “Nosedive,” and “USS Callister.”
Pioneered an interactive feature-length episode, “Bandersnatch,” where viewers choose the story’s path.
Featured high-profile guest stars such as Jon Hamm, Bryce Dallas Howard, and Daniel Kaluuya across its episodes.

title: Post-apocalyptic survival drama about a former sheriff leading a shifting group of survivors through a world overrun by the undead.

clues.text: A post-apocalyptic drama that became one of cable TV’s biggest global hits in the 2010s.
Premiered in 2010 on AMC and ran for 11 seasons, spawning multiple spin-offs and a live aftershow for fan discussion.
Adapted from a black-and-white comic series by Robert Kirkman, with major arcs mirroring the prison and Alexandria communities.
Notorious for shocking character deaths and a barbed-wire-wrapped baseball bat named “Lucille” wielded by a brutal antagonist.
Early seasons follow ex-deputy sheriff Rick Grimes and a Georgia-based group before settling in places like the prison, Terminus, and Alexandria.

title: Period drama about the Crawley family and the household staff in early 20th-century England.

clues.text: A British period drama that became an unlikely global ratings hit for a costume series.
Centers on life both upstairs and downstairs at a grand country estate, spanning the years around World War I into the 1920s.
Debuted in 2010 and ran for six seasons, airing on ITV in the UK and on PBS Masterpiece in the United States.
Created by Julian Fellowes, it’s famed for lavish production values and the Dowager Countess’s razor-sharp one‑liners delivered by Dame Maggie Smith.
Its success led to hit feature films (2019 and 2022) and notable appearances, including Shirley MacLaine joining the cast and a George Clooney cameo in a charity sketch.

title: Character-driven mystery about plane-crash survivors forging bonds and confronting secrets on a perilous island.

clues.text: A mid-2000s network drama that became a global watercooler phenomenon for its serialized, twist-heavy storytelling.
Ran for six seasons from 2004 to 2010 on a major U.S. broadcast network, filmed primarily on Oahu, Hawaii.
Renowned for nonlinear structure—using flashbacks, flash-forwards, and later “flash-sideways” to deepen character arcs.
Its mythology features the DHARMA Initiative, an ominous Smoke Monster, and the recurring numbers 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42.
Focuses on survivors of Oceanic Flight 815 after their plane crashes on a mysterious island.

title: Political thriller about a calculating D.C. power couple clawing their way to the top through manipulation and ambition.

clues.text: Set in Washington, D.C., it portrays cutthroat political deal‑making and media manipulation at the highest levels of government.
One of the first streaming originals to score major Emmy nominations and wins, it helped legitimize binge‑release prestige TV.
Famous for the lead character’s direct-to-camera monologues that frequently break the fourth wall.
Adapted from a 1990 British miniseries and a novel by Michael Dobbs, reimagined for American politics.
Regular cameos by real news anchors appeared throughout, and the central duo—Frank and Claire—treat the capital like their chessboard.

title: Prestige historical drama about a modern monarch balancing family, duty, and politics over decades

clues.text: A lavish period drama exploring the inner workings of the British royal family from the post-war era into the 21st century.
Renowned for meticulous production design and the unique practice of recasting principal roles as characters age.
Its portrayal of real events ignited debates in the UK over historical accuracy and calls for on-screen disclaimers.
Multiple acclaimed actresses have portrayed the central monarch, including Claire Foy, Olivia Colman, and Imelda Staunton.
It dominated the 2021 Primetime Emmys, winning Outstanding Drama Series during the season centered on Charles and Diana.

title: Paranormal investigations led by two FBI agents with clashing beliefs

clues.text: 1990s sci‑fi drama that mixed case-of-the-week mysteries with a larger conspiracy narrative on a major U.S. network.
Originally aired from 1993 to 2002 and later returned for two revival seasons (2016–2018).
Centered on government cover-ups and extraterrestrial life while also featuring memorable standalone ‘monster’ episodes.
Became a cultural phenomenon thanks to the believer–skeptic partnership of David Duchovny and Gillian Anderson’s FBI agents.
Known for the tagline “The truth is out there” and recurring antagonist the Cigarette Smoking Man.

title: Space western about a stoic bounty hunter who protects a mysterious child across a lawless galaxy

clues.text: A live-action space western set in a famous sci‑fi universe, it debuted on a major streaming platform in 2019.
The story follows a helmeted bounty hunter who adheres to a strict warrior creed while roaming the Outer Rim after the Empire’s fall.
It sparked a global craze for a small, mysterious figure nicknamed “Baby Yoda,” whose true name is revealed later on.
Renowned for pioneering LED ‘volume’ stagecraft and episodes directed by filmmakers like Taika Waititi, Bryce Dallas Howard, and Robert Rodriguez.
Centers on Din Djarin and Grogu, with appearances by Ahsoka Tano, Bo-Katan Kryze, and a de-aged Luke Skywalker.

title: Sci-fi adventure about a quirky alien traveler and rotating human companions who protect civilizations across time and space

clues.text: A British science-fiction series spanning decades, with a major revival in 2005 that sparked a new global fandom.
Centers on an eccentric alien journeying with human companions to different times and planets to confront cosmic threats.
The lead character periodically changes appearance and personality through a process that enables new actors to take over the role.
Adventures launch from a blue police box that’s bigger on the inside and known by a four-letter acronym.
Famous elements include the Daleks and Cybermen, episodes like “Blink,” and showrunners such as Russell T Davies and Steven Moffat.

title: Crime family patriarch juggling therapy, marriage, and mob life in suburban New Jersey

clues.text: Widely cited as a landmark series that helped usher in television’s era of complex antiheroes on premium cable.
Aired from 1999 to 2007 on HBO and won dozens of major awards, including multiple Emmys and Peabody honors.
Follows an Italian‑American mob boss who regularly meets with psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Melfi to manage panic attacks.
Its cult‑favorite episode “Pine Barrens” strands two hitmen in snowy woods; Steve Buscemi later both directed and appeared on the show.
The finale’s diner scene ends with an abrupt cut to black while Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’” plays, sparking years of debate.

title: Mockumentary sitcom about three interrelated Los Angeles families led by Jay, Claire, and Mitchell.

clues.text: A single-camera mockumentary comedy that uses talking-head interviews to poke fun at contemporary family life.
Premiered in 2009 and ran for 11 seasons through 2020, becoming a worldwide hit in syndication.
Widely credited with helping normalize LGBTQ family representation on American network television.
Won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series five years in a row, from 2010 to 2014.
Ensemble includes Ed O’Neill, Sofia Vergara, Ty Burrell, Julie Bowen, Jesse Tyler Ferguson, and Eric Stonestreet, with memorable guest turns by Nathan Lane and Elizabeth Banks.

title: Three mischievous presenters tackle cars, stunts, and globe-spanning challenges with celebrity lap times

clues.text: A British factual entertainment series that mixed motoring journalism with comedy and became a worldwide phenomenon.
Relaunched in the early 2000s, it delivered numerous seasons featuring ambitious road-trip specials across multiple continents.
Its test track hosted a recurring segment where famous guests set timed laps in an affordable vehicle.
A silent, helmeted driver known only as “The Stig” set benchmark laps and tested cars.
The trio most associated with its peak—Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May—departed after a 2015 controversy.

title: Post-apocalyptic road drama about a weary smuggler protecting a uniquely resilient teen

clues.text: Prestige survival drama that became one of its network’s biggest streaming launches in 2023.
Adapted from an acclaimed video game franchise developed by Naughty Dog.
Set decades after a cordyceps fungal outbreak, with perilous travel through quarantine zones and ruined cities.
Stars Pedro Pascal and Bella Ramsey, with cameo roles from the game’s Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker.
An early standalone episode titled “Long, Long Time” became a cultural touchstone, and the teen’s suspected immunity drives the mission.

title: Sitcom about five New York friends navigating love, careers, and commitment, guided by a future-tense narrator’s quest for true love

clues.text: American sitcom known for non-linear flashbacks and an ongoing mystery surrounding the lead’s future spouse.
Aired on CBS from 2005 to 2014 for nine seasons, largely set in Manhattan with a favorite neighborhood pub as a hub.
Popularized catchphrases like “suit up!” and recurring gags such as a slap bet and a yellow umbrella motif.
Featured high-profile guest stars including Britney Spears and Katy Perry, with Bob Saget voicing the older narrator.
The finale sparked intense debate by revealing the mother’s fate and the narrator’s ultimate romantic choice.
